lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Cerberus — we're practically family, dog to dog — tell me, by the Styx: what was Socrates actually like when he came down to you? And I'd expect a god like you to do more than bark when the occasion calls for it. You can speak like a human when you want to.
lines.note: Menippus opens with flattery so brazen it's almost an insult. The 'fellow dog' line is a Cynic badge of honour — he's invoking the philosophical kinship of the Cynics (lit. 'the dog people') with complete sincerity and complete cheek.

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: From a distance, Menippus, he looked the part entirely. Steady expression, not obviously afraid, making sure the people standing outside the entrance could see how unafraid he was. But then he leaned in and got a look at the dark — and I gave him a little nip on the ankle with the hemlock to hurry things along — and he went to pieces. Wailing like a baby. Crying about his children.
lines.note: Cerberus delivers this as a matter-of-fact eyewitness report. The hemlock detail is a sly joke: Cerberus administered it, or at least that's how he tells it. No dramatic emphasis — the comedy is entirely in the flatness.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So the man was a sophist after all. No genuine contempt for death.
lines.note: Deadpan verdict. Not triumphant — just noting a fact.

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: No, it wasn't quite that. He could see it was unavoidable, so he put on a show of bravery — as if he weren't being made to do what he had no choice but to do anyway — to impress the audience. That's the whole story with that type, really. Bold and courageous right up to the threshold. The moment they're inside: [pause] a rather more accurate picture emerges.
lines.note: Cerberus is a surprisingly sharp analyst. His verdict is more nuanced than Menippus's — it's not fraud exactly, it's performance. The pause before the last clause is the punchline landing.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And how did I seem to you, coming down?
lines.note: Asked with perfect innocence. He already knows the answer.

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: You were the only one — you and Diogenes before you — who came in a manner worthy of the species. Not under compulsion, not shoved in, but voluntarily, [chuckles] laughing, and telling everyone else to go to hell.
lines.note: The 'species' (γένους) is the Cynic species — dogs. Cerberus is genuinely complimentary and slightly fraternal. 'Telling everyone else to go to hell' is both literal (they're going to Hades) and idiomatic — let it land both ways.
